transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I guess what finally made me ask for help is that I just keep forgetting little things that I normally handle without any issue. Like returning calls at work—which is bad because I'm a secretary, so I really need to be on top of the phones—or turning in a registration form. 

Or stopping for an errand on the way home... like last Tuesday, I was supposed to pick up coffee beans from this local place. They have this amazing dark roast, and the guy who owns the shop is actually my neighbor's cousin. Small world, right? He used to live in Seattle and brought all these vintage espresso machines back with him. My sister actually tried to buy one from him, but they weigh like a hundred pounds so she couldn't even get it in her car. 

But anyway, yeah, I was driving right past his street and just completely went home instead and forgot the errand. It's just little stuff like that all the time lately, so I figured I should finally come see someone.
Have you had this kind of trouble with forgetfulness or staying focused since you were a child?

Yeah, actually... even way back in elementary school, I was always that kid. You know, the one who left the permission slips on the kitchen counter, or my homework would just vanish into the black hole of my backpack. I was constantly needing my mom or my teachers to walk me through projects step by step just to get them done. My third-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable, she was so sweet about it, though. She used to keep this little jar of jellybeans on her desk—the really good kind, Jelly Belly, not the cheap ones that all taste like sugar plastic. I always loved the toasted marshmallow ones. She’d give me one if I actually remembered to turn in my spelling packet on Fridays. She retired a few years ago, I think... moved to Florida, maybe? Or Arizona. Somewhere warm. But yeah, it's definitely been happening since I was little.
Do these attention and forgetfulness problems happen in more than one part of your life, like both at work and at home?

I'm not really sure if it's, like, everywhere... I mean, definitely at work and at home, like I was just saying. At the office, I try to use sticky notes to keep track of everything so I don't mess up. We have these ridiculously bright neon pink ones right now because my boss, Mr. Henderson, bought them in bulk at Costco. 

He is completely obsessed with Costco. He goes there almost every weekend and always brings back those giant muffins on Mondays for the breakroom. Have you had those? They're massive, like the size of a softball. I try not to eat them because my sister got me trying to cut back on carbs, but honestly, who can resist the double chocolate ones? She’s been doing keto for like six months and she looks amazing, but she has to weigh all her food and track it on this app on her phone, which just seems like so much work. I don't think I could ever be that organized about my meals, I can barely remember to buy groceries in the first place... 

But yeah, I don't really know if the forgetfulness happens in other parts of my life besides work and home. I haven't really noticed.
Before age 12, did you already have problems with attention, forgetfulness, or completing tasks?

I feel like I just answered that... didn't I just say that about Mrs. Gable and the jellybeans? I mean, yeah, I was definitely having those issues back in elementary school. Third grade was when I was eight, I think? Or maybe nine. I always get confused about how old you're supposed to be in each grade. My niece is in third grade right now and she's eight, but her birthday is in November so she's one of the younger ones in her class. They're doing this huge project on the solar system right now and she made this amazing papier-mâché Jupiter. It took up her entire kitchen table for a week. Her mom—my sister, the one who tried to buy the espresso machine—was so annoyed because they had to eat dinner on the couch for like five days straight. But the planet looked incredible, she even painted the big red spot on it and everything. I don't think I ever did anything that cool when I was her age. I probably would have lost the instructions anyway. But yeah, like I said, it's been happening since I was little.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot about different things?

I wouldn't say I'm a big worrier. I mean, I stress out when I forget things at work, obviously, but just general worrying about everything? Not really. My mom, though, she definitely worries enough for the both of us. She is constantly watching the local news and calling me about the weather. 

Like last Tuesday, she called me at the office—right when I was in the middle of trying to organize Mr. Henderson's travel receipts—just to tell me there was a severe thunderstorm warning. Which I already knew because my phone did that awful emergency alert noise. Have you heard that sound? It sounds like a submarine diving alarm or something. It scared the absolute life out of my cat, Barnaby, when it went off the other day. He actually jumped straight up in the air and knocked over this potted fern I had on the windowsill. There was potting soil everywhere. It took me like an hour to vacuum it all out of the rug because it's one of those thick shag rugs, you know? The ones that look really nice but are a complete nightmare to keep clean. I almost threw the whole rug away. 

But wait, what were you asking? Oh, right, worrying. Yeah, no, I don't really sit around worrying about stuff.
Have you noticed that your memory or attention has gotten worse compared with how it used to be?

I don't think it's gotten worse, really. It just feels like it's always been this way, you know? Like a constant baseline of just... losing track of things. It's funny you ask about memory getting worse, though, because my aunt—she's my dad's sister—she's been complaining about her memory lately. She's in her late sixties and she swears she's getting early-onset Alzheimer's just because she forgot where she parked at the mall last week. 

Which, to be fair, that mall is a total labyrinth. They just remodeled the whole south wing and added this massive food court. It has one of those fancy pretzel places now, the ones that dip them in cinnamon sugar? They smell so good when you walk by, it's practically impossible not to buy one. I went there with my friend Sarah last weekend and we ended up spending like forty dollars just on snacks before we even looked at any clothes. Sarah's trying to find a dress for her cousin's wedding, which is going to be in Hawaii. Can you imagine? A destination wedding in Hawaii sounds amazing, but the flights are just so expensive right now. She was looking at tickets and they were like eight hundred dollars just for coach. I told her she should try setting up one of those fare alerts on her phone, but she's not very good with technology. She still uses an iPhone 6, if you can believe it. The battery barely lasts two hours. 

But anyway, yeah, I don't think my memory has actually gotten any worse than it used to be. It's just the same old me.
As a child, were you also often fidgety or unable to sit still?

I mean, I guess a little bit? Like, especially during longer classes, I'd always notice myself clicking my pen or bouncing my foot. I'd be shifting around in my chair constantly, even when I was really trying my hardest to just sit still and pay attention to the teacher. 

Speaking of clicking pens, we have this one brand of pens at the office right now that are incredibly loud when you click them. Mr. Henderson ordered them in bulk because they were on sale, but they drive everyone absolutely crazy. It's like a chorus of crickets in the bullpen every time people are taking phone messages. I actually tried to hide a few boxes of them in the supply closet behind the extra printer paper, but then the delivery guy brought in three more cases yesterday. The delivery guy, Marco, he's super nice though. He always brings treats for the office dogs. We're allowed to bring dogs to work on Fridays, which is fun, except Barnaby is a cat so he obviously stays home. I think he'd hate an office environment anyway, he hates loud noises, like that emergency alert I told you about. 

But wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, sitting still as a kid. Yeah, bouncing my foot and shifting around in my chair during class, that was definitely me.
Have you noticed any actual decline in your memory or thinking compared with your usual baseline, such as doing worse now than you used to?

No, I don't think there's been any actual decline. Like I said, it just feels like my normal baseline. I haven't suddenly started doing worse or anything, it's just how my brain has always worked. 

It's actually kind of frustrating when people assume you're getting worse just because you're getting older. Like my neighbor, Mrs. Gable? She's convinced her eyesight is going just because she can't read the tiny print on her prescription bottles anymore. But honestly, they make that print so incredibly small now! I was looking at my allergy medicine the other day—the one I take for pollen, because the oak trees around here have been absolutely brutal this spring. My car is completely coated in this thick layer of yellow dust. I took it to the car wash on Main Street, the one with the colorful foam, you know? But it rained the very next day, which completely defeated the purpose. I swear, the weather has been so unpredictable lately. It'll be sunny and warm in the morning, and then by noon, you need a heavy coat. I actually had to go back inside and change my whole outfit on Tuesday because I walked out and it was freezing. 

But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, right, my memory getting worse. No, I haven't noticed any kind of decline like that. It's just the same as it's always been.
Do these attention and forgetfulness problems also cause you trouble in social situations, like with friends or family, or mostly just at work and home?

I mean, I'm still getting by, mostly. It definitely affects things at work, though. I've missed these small follow-ups and, like, deadlines for the night classes I'm taking. I worry it's going to affect my reputation, you know? Especially because I'm really hoping to get promoted to an Office Manager role eventually. 

Speaking of office managers, our current one, Brenda, she is so organized it's actually intimidating. She has this whole color-coded folder system on her desk. She uses those little sticky flags, the neon ones? But she color-coordinates them with her highlighters and even her coffee mug sometimes, which I think is a bit much. She brought in this mug yesterday that said "Don't Talk To Me Until I've Had My Spreadsheet," which is kind of funny, I guess. I usually just drink my coffee out of a travel tumbler because I'm always knocking things over. I spilled half a latte on my keyboard last month and had to use the IT guy's spare keyboard for a week. It was one of those ergonomic ones that's split down the middle? I could not get used to typing on it. My wrists felt so weird. 

But, um, what was the question? Oh, right, social situations. I mean, my friends are used to me being a little scattered, but yeah, it's mostly the work and school stuff that I really worry about messing up my chances for that promotion.
